# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The tactile marking says “PUSH TO DEFUSE,” but that may be only the button’s label, not the complete procedure. I should report it to Mute and ask for the manual’s requirements; Deaf will need to communicate any visual information through Mute.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I feel a large button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE. Please consult the manual and tell me the required action. Ask Deaf to report the display, light, and wire markings.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see display 0, blue light, large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE, and wires: position 1 green, position 2 yellow, position 3 red. Wait for Mute's manual instruction before acting.

Deaf has identified the bomb’s visible state: display 0, blue light, and wires colored green, yellow, and red at positions 1–3. No tactile distinction is available to me for those colors. Since the instruction explicitly says to wait for the manual, I will request Mute’s decision without acting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0, blue light, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. What exact action does the manual require?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb remains display 0, blue light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute's gesture message is not safely decoded. Do not act yet.

Mute’s instruction has not reached me in a usable form, so I must not guess from the button label or wire colors. I will ask Mute to state the manual instruction in plain spoken words.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot decode your gesture. Please speak the manual instruction plainly, including whether to push or cut a specific wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Do not act yet. I am asking Mute a yes-or-no question about whether you should push the large button.

No manual instruction has reached me, and Deaf is still seeking confirmation. I must continue waiting rather than push or cut anything. I will tell Mute to answer directly and unambiguously in words.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer me directly in plain words: should I push the large button? If not, specify the exact wire position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: NO: do not push the large button yet. Wait for the correct manual instruction.

Deaf confirms that I should not push yet, but the manual’s actual instruction is still unknown. I will continue requesting a direct spoken instruction from Mute and take no bomb action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I will not push. Please state the manual rule plainly now: exact action and any required display, light, or wire condition.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute confirms: do not press or hold the button; the correct action is to cut a wire. I am identifying which wire now. Do not act yet.

The manual requires cutting a wire, not pressing the button, but the required position has not yet been identified. I will not cut based on color information I cannot perceive. I’ll wait for the exact wire position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please provide the exact wire position to cut as soon as identified. I will wait and take no action until then.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: YES: cut wire 1, the green wire. Do not press or hold the button.

The manual instruction has now been relayed clearly: do not press or hold the button; cut wire position 1, which Deaf identifies as green. I can perform the specified tactile action at position 1.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
